# Reciprocal source review: uncovered-head retirement and path constant

2026-10-11 17:17 UTC. Verdict: COMPONENT PASS for the exact sources below. Read-only review by the active Light EFT owner; no child, compiler, kernel replay or independent whole-paper audit was performed for this review.

## Uncovered-head source

I read the complete source and its covered-head saturation/substitution dependencies. The proof uses the original-source entry convention throughout. Saturation gives exactly the endpoint label set. An uncovered endpoint contributes no label; hence any covered dart head in the route must have the start's label. If the dart needs the original-source first-entry branch, that head is the start vertex. Legal augmentation transports both the preceding prefix and this dart to original reachability; DAG antisymmetry then contradicts the dart's distinct endpoints. Every surviving dart therefore meets the source-independent branches of the filter.

The resulting old route is substituted literally for the new dart and introduces no extra chain label. The normalized-distance equality splits on original reachability, preserving the convention of zero for originally unreachable pairs. Legality is retained where needed. The potential is the unchanged raw objective. The final necessary own-excess test covers the uncovered-head case here and the already proved covered-head case; no uncovered candidate category is silently discarded. Monotonicity plus the endpoint lower bound make retirement persistent in a later legal superstate. There is no quantitative marginal bound or changing-source optimum assumption.

## Exact directed-path constant

With singleton chains, every original reachable pair is important, preprocessing is empty, and distance is the number of visited vertices. For a forward candidate i<j the affected rectangle is precisely s<=i and t>=j. The actual reduction is j-i-1, giving the exact raw drop (i+1)(j-i-1)(n-j). The correspondence with triples a>=1,b>=0,c>=1 and a+b+c=n is exhaustive. Positive maxima for n>=3 have balanced factors, so at n=3q the maximum is q^3. Consequently the proposed inequality with an additive n term requires C>=27 as q tends to infinity; the explicit finite q choice in the note is correct. It is a constant obstruction only, not a refutation for arbitrary absolute C, and it is stated in the supplied-chain context rather than asserted for the canonical cover constructor. The final-window/threshold warning follows and is appropriately qualified.

No mathematical blocker found. These findings do not resolve the remaining uniform phase-amortization or original paper theorem.

# Reciprocal source review: insertion-tail demand support

2026-10-11 17:22 UTC. COMPONENT PASS for analysis/ChainTailRowSupport.lean,
SHA256 b4c668ad6869b45ec936aa6e52921dc9cb9c0914e16e26d720de1ef2ec6e01d1.
All139 lines were read. This is source-only review by the active Light owner;
no compiler, child or whole-paper audit was used.

The elimination lemma replaces the entire remaining suffix when its first
inserted dart is found, rather than pretending the replacement ends at that
dart's head. The old tail-to-target route is genuinely attained, and saturation
puts its chain labels among those of the two endpoints, which already occur
in the replaced suffix. Existing legal saturated-route transfer supplies the
same original source's filter because both demands share the literal important
target. Noninserted darts preserve their old validity; recursive append retains
label-set inclusion. There is no claim about transporting an unsaturated
minimum.

For a genuinely improved important demand, the attained new minimizing route
must contain a newly valid dart. The proof extracts the actual inserted pair
from its augmented-edge membership. Legality transports both prefix and suffix
back to original reachability, so important-pair inheritance proves that the
literal insertion tail and original target form an important demand. If that
demand were saturated, the previous whole-suffix substitution would contradict
the observed strict improvement. Thus its positive excess is genuinely proved.

Summing uses the existing attained improved-pair witness for the unchanged raw
potential. The final saturated-row result uses antitonicity and this necessary
live-tail condition. All outgoing legal candidates, including uncovered heads,
are covered. The graph remains a DAG with fixed original-source selectors;
no row-saving lower bound, positive-excess minimum inheritance, candidate-volume
bound or quantitative phase amortization is smuggled into the conclusion.
No blocker found at this scope. Owner strict/audit/replay/CI gates remain separate.
